text.p: Programme of matches in the German first division over the Easter period:

Duisburg (14) v Hamburg (12). A game unlikely to raise heartbeats outside of Hamburg and Duisburg. Both teams are in the lower half of the table with little to play for except avoiding getting too close to the relegation zone.

St. Pauli (16) v Borussia Dortmund (4). Dortmund suffered their first home defeat of the season last weekend and need three points to keep up their championship challenge. After two consecutive defeats, the reigning champions cannot afford to lose against a team who have won just four of 11 home games. "We have to win," said coach Ottmar Hitzfeld who must do without wing-back Stefan Reuter and defender Juergen Kohler (both suspended).

VfB Stuttgart (2) v 1860 Munich (8). Stuttgart have been scoring goals with ease in the last few weeks and have a remarkable goal difference of 59-25 (+34). They struck five past 1860 earlier in the season and the Stuttgart stadium will have a sell-out 53,000 crowd for the south German derby.

Bochum (6) v Cologne (9). With just three points separating the teams this is a crucial game in the battle for UEFA Cup places. Promoted Bochum have a good record at home, losing just one of 12 games.

Bayern Munich (1) v Werder Bremen (10). In past seasons this has been a top-of-the-table clash but Werder have struggled to make an impact this term. Bayern need to forget their internal battles and are expected to have striker Juergen Klinsmann back in their ranks after suspension.

Arminia Bielefeld (11) v Karlsruhe (7). Karlsruhe need to get their campaign for a place in Europe back on track after a 2-0 home defeat to Bayern last Sunday. But promoted Bielefeld are a much tougher opponent than they were in the first half of the season.
Bayer Leverkusen (3) v Schalke (5). A clash which is important to both teams. Leverkusen won 2-1 in Gelsenkirchen earlier in the season.

Hansa Rostock (17) v Freiburg (18). A real relegation battle. Seven points separate two teams so the result is crucial. Points are more important to Hansa since it will be extraordinary if Freiburg avoid the drop.
Borussia Moenchengladbach (13) v Fortuna Duesseldorf (15). Moenchengladbach are on a high after beating Dortmund but they are still too close to the relegation zone for comfort.
